_README: THE PERSON FILE — layer ① of four. Answers: WHO is applying?
Copy to users/<you>.json and fill in. That copy is gitignored (it holds
real contact details); THIS file is the tracked shape.
① users/<you>.json          WHO      <- you are here
② vaults/<you>.json         WHAT     the VAULT (see vaults/you.example.json)
name: Your Full Name

contact.emailPolicy: ⭐ DEFAULT = you@yourdomain.com. Use it on EVERY resume, cover letter, and application unless the person explicitly says otherwise in that conversation. Do not ask; do not deliberate; just use it.

emailRules._note: Exactly ONE address is the default. An agent uses it automatically, every time. The others exist to be RECOGNIZED, not selected.
emailRules.default: you@yourdomain.com — professional, on your own domain. THE DEFAULT, always.
emailRules.studioContext: you@yourcompany.com — ONLY if you have a SEPARATE company address AND are applying as the company. Omit this key if your default already IS the company domain.
emailRules.personal: you@gmail.com — a VALID address, just not the preferred one. Recorded as a reference/recovery address (job boards, signups, 2FA). NEVER auto-select it on a resume or cover letter.
emailRules.⚠whyItIsRecorded: It is listed so an agent can RECOGNIZE it — spot it on an old resume and flag it, or match a job-board account. NOT so an agent can use it. Presence in this file is not permission. Only the person naming it, in that conversation, overrides the default.

vaultQuery._note: The vault is queried BY TRACK. Pick the track matching the listing, read roleTracks.<track>.angle, then select claims whose `tracks` include that track — ranked TRACK-SPECIFIC FIRST, then by `strength` (lead > solid > supporting).

identity.headline: What you are, in six words
identity.voice: One-line summary. Full personality → characterVoice below; application prose SSOT → vault voice.
identity.background: Optional short bio. Prefer characterVoice.personality.backgroundFlavor as the deeper SSOT — keep this one line or omit.

characterVoice._ssot: THE ONE person-level voice-design area. Set personality, contrast, and all cross-register pointers here. Application prose itself lives only in vaults/<you>.json#voice; do not duplicate tone rules in profiles.
_editOrder: Set personality and optional partner contrast here.
Optionally add a public Voice Seed pointer after the local layers are complete. Voice Seed is a map/integration point, not a duplicate source of resume voice.

personality.coreDrive: One sentence: what they are trying to make / why they work.
personality.catchphrase: Optional short line that captures them.

contrastWithPartner._note: OPTIONAL — use when two people from one studio both apply. Prevents flattened 'same voice' résumés.
ILeadWith: What makes THIS applicant sound like themselves
TheyLeadWith: What the partner leads with — so agents do not copy it here
neverConflate: Specialty that belongs only to one person

registers.socialPersonal: (optional path to a socials format-manifest voice string)
registers.discordVisual: (optional path to a Discord STYLE-SPEC — emoji/visual only)

emojiPreferences._note: Social/Discord only — never on ATS resume PDFs.

sampleLines.coverLetterOpen: 1–2 example openings in their real voice.
sampleLines.resumeSummaryFlavor: How a summary line should feel.

brandTheme._note: Your fallback palette — used when a target company gives no usable color signal. Otherwise the palette is derived from THEIR brand CSS (see _job-listings/<Track>/theme.json).
brandTheme.name: Your Brand
brandTheme.⚠paletteRule: No brown, no mustard, no lime. Amber has NO readable dark form on white paper — it turns brown. On light, hand the amber role to another hue. Enforced on every export; see themes/PALETTE-RULES.md.

profiles._note: ONE profile per person. There are NO per-track profile files — the per-role framing lives in the VAULT at roleTracks.<track>.angle.

hardFacts.note: Frequently-needed facts so an agent never has to ask. A SUMMARY — the vault is the source of truth.
hardFacts.tenure: State YOUR tenure explicitly. ⚠ If your company is older than your time at it, say both numbers and never let a resume blur them.
hardFacts.tools: The tools you actually use, grouped.
⚠unverifiedToolsNote: UNVERIFIED ≠ ABSENT. This list means only: NOBODY HAS ASKED.
These are neither claimable NOR a gap.
If a listing needs one -> ASK THE PERSON FIRST.
If they have it  -> write it into the vault's `skills` and USE it.
If they don't    -> only THEN is it a gap; set status `confirmed-absent`.
This exists because a flat blocklist cannot tell 'we asked and they don't have it'
from 'nobody ever checked' — so it silently becomes the second one. Two industry-
standard DCC apps were forbidden on real resumes for months while the applicants
had YEARS of experience with each. Nobody had ever asked.
The vault's doNotClaim block is a VERIFICATION LEDGER with a per-tool `status`,
precisely so this failure is structurally impossible. Validate it:
